$comment: Rule catalog — evidence requirements, applicability declaration, equivalences. Standards 1, 9, 15, 18, 19.

rules.title: The project declares its regimes
rules.description: project-policy.yml declares which of the five regimes describe the project, and every not-applicable classification carries a reason and a revisitWhen condition.
rules.rationale: A standard that applies to everything applies to nothing, and a not-applicable classification with no revisit condition is a permanent exemption wearing a temporary label.
rules.remediation: Add the mathematics.regimes list, and give every not-applicable classification a reason and the event that would end it.
rules.$assuranceNote: Establishes that the declaration exists and is well-formed. It cannot tell whether the declaration is honest — a project that declares no formal regime while carrying Lean files is caught by formal.status-declared, but one that simply describes itself wrongly is not.

rules.title: Evidence types come from the closed vocabulary
rules.description: Every evidence entry declares a type from the nine tokens of Standard 19 R2.
rules.rationale: Each type carries a ceiling — the highest claim rank it can support alone. An open-ended type field would let 'verification' or 'validation' carry whatever ceiling the writer intended.
rules.remediation: Replace the type with the closest token from Standard 19 R2's table.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact. The property is entirely about the text of the field.

rules.title: Evidence points at something that exists
rules.description: Every path-shaped evidence reference resolves to a file in the repository, with any anchor suffix removed before resolution.
rules.rationale: Evidence that points at nothing is an assertion. The practical test is whether someone else could reach the same conclusion without trusting the claimant.
rules.remediation: Commit the artifact, or correct the path. Citations are permitted and are reported as unverifiable by an offline checker.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact about existence at the cited path. What is in the file, and whether it establishes the claim, is outside the reach of this or any other check here.

rules.title: Findings are labelled by how they were obtained
rules.description: Every finding carries one of OBSERVED, INFERRED, CONFIRMED_BY_OWNER, or UNKNOWN, and no heuristic detection is labelled OBSERVED.
rules.rationale: A heuristic reported as observed is the tool fabricating certainty about its own output — the same error as presenting numerical evidence as proof, committed by the checker instead of the mathematician.
rules.remediation: Label phrase-matching and pattern-based detections INFERRED. Reserve OBSERVED for what was read directly from a file.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks that every finding carries a label from the vocabulary. That each label is the right one for how the finding was produced is enforced by a test over the detectors, not by this rule at run time.

rules.title: An unevaluated rule is never reported as passing
rules.description: No result in the compliance envelope carries status passed with disposition not-evaluated, and no unevaluated rule counts toward the compliance score.
rules.rationale: This is the rule everything else protects. A false red has a complainant; a false green has none, by construction.
rules.remediation: This is a check on the tooling. A failure means the evaluator or the compliance engine has a defect and must be fixed, not configured around.
rules.$assuranceNote: Exact, and unusual in that its subject is this tool's own output rather than the project's mathematics.

rules.title: An asserted equivalence names what proves it
rules.description: An Equivalences entry claiming iff names a claim that proves the equivalence, and that claim resolves and is at proved rank.
rules.rationale: Asserting iff where only one direction is proved is a silent strengthening, and the equivalence is itself a claim needing a proof like any other.
rules.remediation: Record the direction actually proved — implies or implied-by — or prove the equivalence and cite the claim that does.
rules.$assuranceNote: Checks the declared direction and that the naming claim exists at proved rank. Whether the two statements really are equivalent is mathematics.

rules.title: A counterexample is never hidden
rules.description: A discovered counterexample is not recorded, or the claim it refutes is not demoted.
rules.rationale: Hiding a counterexample does not make a claim true; it makes the record false. Narrowing a domain after finding one is legitimate — the difference is entirely in whether the counterexample is recorded.
rules.remediation: Record the counterexample as evidence and demote the claim in the same change. Where the domain is narrowed instead, record that as a history entry.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, and not for lack of effort: a suppressed counterexample leaves no trace in the repository, so there is nothing for a check to find. The defence is that Standard 18 requires failed routes to be preserved, making deletion a visible act rather than an absence.

rules.title: Failed experiments that undermine a hypothesis are never discarded
rules.description: A run whose result tells against a hypothesis is deleted or omitted from the record.
rules.rationale: What remains in the repository is then a record of everything that supported the conclusion, which is a different and much more flattering thing than a record of what happened.
rules.remediation: Restore the run, or record what it was and what it showed. Preserved does not mean prominent.
rules.$assuranceNote: No detector, for the same structural reason as evidence.hidden-counterexample. Established by review against the preserved-failures location Standard 18 requires.
